title: The Straw, the Coal and the Bean
text:
An old woman in a village was cooking a dish of beans. To get the fire going quickly, she lit it with a handful of straw. As she poured the beans into the pot, one bean slipped to the floor beside a piece of straw, and a moment later a glowing coal jumped out of the fire and landed next to them.

The three had each narrowly escaped death, so they decided to stay together and travel to a foreign country. Soon they came to a small brook with no bridge. The straw had an idea. It would lay itself across the water, and the others could walk over on it.

The coal, which was hot-tempered, went first and tripped boldly onto the straw. But halfway across, it heard the water rushing below. It grew frightened and stopped, and stood there unable to go forward or back. The straw caught fire under it, burned through and broke apart. The coal hissed into the water and went out.

The bean, still on the bank, laughed so hard at the sight that it burst. A wandering tailor who was resting by the brook took pity on it and sewed it up. He only had black thread, and that, the story says, is why beans have a black seam.
lesson: A shared plan can fail because one member freezes halfway through. Once a team commits to a crossing, hesitation in the middle is often worse than either going on or turning back.
people: A straw, a coal, a bean, a tailor
source: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 18, The Straw, the Coal and the Bean
